title: Finite Game-Tree Strategy Induces An Outcome
body_html:
Finite Game-Tree Strategy Induces An Outcome

For a finite perfect-information, no-chance GameTree, a strategy selects one child at every decision node. Recursively following those selections reaches a leaf and therefore determines its payoff vector.

Finiteness and nonempty children are structural properties of GameTree, so this specialization needs no separate termination certificate. It is narrower than the general Arena claim in [[game_theory.extensive_game.core.strategy_profile_induced_outcome]], where cycles and non-player-controlled transitions are permitted.

References

  • [MFoGT, Section 6.2.2] Laraki, Renault, and Sorin, Mathematical Foundations of Game Theory. In a finite perfect-information tree without Nature, a strategy profile selects a unique terminal path.

noncomputable def outcome (σ : Strategy N U) : GameTree N U → (N → U)
  | Leaf p => p
  | Node m h t => outcome σ (σ m h t).val
termination_by g => g.size

  have hmem := (σ m h t).property
